initiative.title: Taskset Board Attention Workspace
initiative.summary: Implement the accepted taskset_attention_workspace direction so the Taskset Board opens with explainable attention lanes, a keyboard-first switcher, and a relation detail path before the full 49-taskset fallback list.

taskset.summary: Source-mutating implementation of the accepted Taskset Board IA RFC: attention lane derivation, taskset switcher, relation detail panel, and beta/UX evidence for desktop, mobile, keyboard, reduced-motion, and recovery states.

tasks.title: Implement Taskset Board attention workspace assets
tasks.goal: Convert the Taskset Board from a whole-board-first scan into an attention workspace with explainable lanes, taskset switcher, and relation detail while preserving the full searchable board fallback.
tasks.scope: Source mutation is allowed only inside the declared UI state, UI asset, design asset, and focused test files. Do not change task/claim SSoT files, write APIs, dispatcher behavior, or unrelated console views.
acceptance: The Taskset Board first viewport exposes attention lanes for active claims, guarded or interrupted work, stale or missing evidence, recently changed tasksets, and ready next-action candidates before the all-tasksets fallback.
Lane membership is derived from named schema fields and each card shows a visible reason label; state is never color-only.
A keyboard-first taskset switcher supports known-target retrieval by id, title, alias, task id, and owner, with empty state and selected state.
A relation detail panel preserves the existing operator_attention_graph semantics: taskset state, claim path, evidence freshness, graph or child context, and command readiness.
Repeated lane, switcher, relation detail, state chip, and evidence preview surfaces are implemented as design assets or explicitly classified as one_off_for_now in closeout evidence.
The existing Taskset Board API remains read-only and page/server files stay focused on data wiring and composition.

units.title: Add Taskset Board attention lane schema and workspace UI
units.context: TASK-AR-610 accepted taskset_attention_workspace after OAG beta evidence showed 49 tasksets make whole-board scanning and focus traversal too long.
units.scope: Source mutation is limited to declared UI state, UI asset, design asset, focused test, verification evidence, and review-index files. Do not change task/claim SSoT files, write APIs, dispatcher behavior, or unrelated console views.

assetization.rule: Reuse existing pass/warn/block/info/active semantic tokens first; add aliases only in token definitions if lane states cannot be distinguished.
Keyboard-first typeahead with result count, selected state, empty state, and jump target.
Segmented or tab-like control with count, focus state, and non-color cue.
Domain lane combining taskset identity, claim state, evidence freshness, command readiness, and membership reason.
Extend or reuse patternAttentionRelationPanel and evidence preview responsibilities without duplicating relation chip/card markup.
Allowed only for the first beta cycle; promote or remove before a third use.

steps: Read the RFC assetization table and current tasksets_board API tests.
Derive attention lane data in ui_state.py from the named schema fields without writing task or claim records.
Add reusable ui_design_assets helpers for quick switcher, lane filter, attention lane, or relation detail only where current helpers cannot cover the surface.
Wire ui_console_assets.py so the first Taskset Board viewport renders attention lanes, switcher, and relation detail before the full all-tasksets fallback.
Preserve expanded/collapsed full board behavior and command proposal path for adding tasks.
Add focused state and UI tests for lane reasons, switcher empty and selected states, keyboard/focus anchors, mobile CSS anchors, and existing claim-summary behavior.
Run W4a verification commands and record evidence.
acceptance: Active, guarded, interrupted, stale or missing evidence, recently changed, ready next action, empty lane, and no active claim paths are visibly labelled.
Keyboard traversal reaches lane controls, switcher, active card, relation detail, and all-tasksets fallback without tabbing through every taskset first.
At 390x844, lanes, switcher, and detail stack without document-level horizontal overflow.
Reduced-motion mode removes movement-dependent meaning if transitions are introduced.
No raw color, spacing, radius, shadow, or type literals are introduced outside token definitions.
The implementation preserves existing /api/tasksets_board aliases and task.create proposal-only behavior.
units.handoff: Report changed helpers, lane derivation fields, assetization classification, focused tests, beta evidence dependency, and any remaining one-off or schema gaps.
units.stop_condition: Stop after the attention workspace implementation is source-mutated, tested, self-verified, and ready for independent W4b verification.

tasks.title: Run Taskset Board attention workspace beta and UX evaluation
tasks.goal: Verify the attention workspace through user-like beta actions, keyboard traversal, mobile and desktop viewport checks, reduced-motion review, recovery states, and BTC-style defect routing.
tasks.scope: Evaluation and evidence only. Do not mutate UI source files in this task. Implementation defects become BTC-style follow-up candidates or a new claimed implementation task.
acceptance: Beta evidence records exact clicked or typed actions for unknown-target discovery, known-target retrieval, relation detail inspection, and all-tasksets fallback.
Keyboard traversal is exercised from route entry through lane controls, switcher, card selection, relation detail, and fallback list.
Recovery attempts cover empty lane, stale evidence, blocked command, interrupted claim, expired claim, and no active claim states.
Desktop and mobile viewport notes include environment, viewport, data state, expected result, observed result, and pass/fail status.
Reduced-motion behavior and non-color-only state cues are reviewed.
Every visible defect gets a BTC-TSAW failure id with reproduction path and assetization class.

units.title: Record Taskset Board attention workspace beta and UX evidence
units.context: The Owner asked for UI/UX improvement loops that include beta-tester and evaluator evidence rather than screenshot-only completion claims.
units.scope: Record exploratory evidence only. Do not patch UI source files in this unit.
steps: Launch or inspect the local UI surface for the implemented Taskset Board route.
Execute unknown-target discovery from the first viewport and record the selected lane reason.
Type a known taskset id or title fragment into the switcher and jump to the matching detail.
Traverse by keyboard through lane controls, switcher, selected card, relation detail, and all-tasksets fallback.
Repeat the main path at desktop and 390x844 mobile viewport.
Exercise empty lane, stale evidence, blocked command, interrupted claim, expired claim, and no active claim recovery states.
Review reduced-motion and non-color-only state cues.
Assign BTC-TSAW ids to every visible defect and refresh evidence index.
acceptance: Evidence lists exact action path, viewport, data state, expected result, observed result, pass/fail status, and screenshot or trace reference when available.
Recovery and edge states are attempted, not merely listed.
No UI source files are changed by the evaluation unit.
Every actionable defect has an owner and assetization class.
units.handoff: Report beta paths, defects, accessibility and responsive findings, BTC-TSAW ids, and whether the next UI/UX cycle needs design exploration or implementation refinement.
units.stop_condition: Stop after beta and UX evidence are complete and ready for independent W4b verification.
